name: Training and fine-tuning connectome-constrained visual models for new tasks (FlyVis Lappalainen et al. Nature 2024; Cowley et al. Nature 2024 knockout training of LC neurons; Shiu et al. Nature 2024 whole-brain FlyWire model; task-optimized fly vision models 2023-2026)

inputs_state_output: [1] FlyVis (the project's core): input = rendered Sintel video on 721 hexagonal photoreceptor columns (R1-R8), 19 frames at 24 Hz, integration dt 20 ms; state = recurrent membrane voltages of 45,669 neurons (65 cell-type parameter groups, 1,513,231 connections); output = instantaneous voltages of 34 'output' cell types of medulla and downstream (incl. T4a-d/T5a-d) fed to a 2-layer conv decoder (34 maps -> 8 -> 3 channels, 5x5) that predicts optic flow; the decoder 'cannot by itself detect motion'. No strong appearance branch: one branch only. [2] Cowley 1-to-1 network: input = 10 most recent frames (~300 ms) of a reconstructed 64x228 grey image showing a fictive female on a white background; vision CNN (3 conv layers, 32 filters, shared over time) -> 16-d embedding per frame -> LC bottleneck (dense 64 -> 23 ReLU units, one per silenced LC/LPLC type, reading all 10 frames, so units integrate over time) -> decision MLP (3x128) -> 6 behavioural outputs (forward/lateral/angular velocity, P(sine), P(Pfast), P(Pslow)). Not connectome-constrained; only the bottleneck identity of units is biological. [3] Shiu: whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire network (127,400 FlyWire neurons, materialisation 630), input = Poisson stimulation of chosen sensory neurons (taste, mechanosensory), output = firing of motor/descending neurons; no visual input, no training. [4] Tschopp 2018: hexagonal-lattice conv model of the motion pathway initialised from Takemura connectome, 164 unconstrained decoder neurons, input DAVIS-2016 videos, output = position (x,y) and velocity of the single annotated object. [5] NeuroMechFly v2: frozen best FlyVis model per eye at 500 Hz, readout of the 34 T-shaped output types, object = ommatidia with z-scored activity (vs an empty-arena baseline) above 7; single leading fly, no distractors. [8] Frozen FlyVis on moving 64x64 drawing patches, 57 non-input types x 3 statistics x 8 trajectories = 1,368-d descriptor, cosine nearest-legend match. Ours: two branches - strong frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign appearance per real detection region (cosine to snapped exemplar, previous target, bank, 32 PCA products) and weak FlyVis branch (68 regional features = 34 output types + 6-neighbour means from a bounded grey crop, recurrent state over exemplar+search frames), fused in gradient boosting for identity, then a full-box transfer gate. None of the sources has a strong appearance base plus a fly branch; [1], [4], [5] are motion/position of a single object; [2] decodes behaviour from one rendered object; nothing addresses which of several similar detections is the target.
fusion_and_training: [1] End-to-end BPTT of connectome model + decoder with Adam (beta 0.9/0.999), batch 4, lr 5e-5 -> 5e-6 in ten steps, ~250,000 iterations; FIXED from connectome: synapse counts N per type pair and offset (2,355 values) and signs (604, from transmitter predictions); TRAINED: 65 resting potentials, 65 time constants (clamped >= dt), 604 non-negative per-type-pair scaling factors alpha (init 0.01 x average count) = 734 free parameters (matches local _meta.yaml: syn_count/sign requires_grad false; bias/time_const/syn_strength true). Separate resting-potential activity regulariser (lambda_V 0.1, 150,000 iterations). 50 models from the same initialisation = 50 local optima. [2] Knockout training: all perturbed + control sessions pooled; for a sample from a male with LC type k silenced, model LC unit k is set to 0 by a mask; SGD lr 1e-3, momentum 0.7, batch 288 balanced over 24 conditions (12 samples each) and song type; early stopping on forward-velocity validation; Keras default init. Adding unperturbed 'slack' units (45 instead of 23) did not help and, in the extreme, lets the network ignore the knocked-out units - an explicit statement that capacity elsewhere lets a model bypass the constrained units (analogous to a strong branch starving a weak one). [3] No training: all parameters from literature, weights = FlyWire synapse counts x sign x W_syn, single free parameter W_syn = 0.275 mV chosen so that 100 Hz sugar GRN gives ~80% of maximal MN9 firing. [4] Adam with weight decay, 30,000 iterations; sign constraints enforced by projected update theta' = sign(theta0)|theta|; configurations: connectome-initialised trained, +40% noise, connectome weights frozen (only biases and decoder trained), random MSRA init with connectome signs, +noise, older connectome. [5] No training of FlyVis; heuristic threshold readout. [7] Full AdamW training of a connectome-motif architecture with learned scalar gates and a zero-initialised low-frequency branch. [8] No training of FlyVis. Ours (prepared, not run): scripts/z13_core_identity_20261026.py trains the same 734 parameters (nodes_bias lr 1e-4, nodes_time_const and edges_syn_strength lr 5e-6, attraction penalty to the stock solution, clamp after step) + one logit scale, 300 steps x 8 episodes on fit84, through a differentiable closed-form ridge target filter; MASA is not in the loop. No source trains a fly branch jointly with a frozen strong appearance model, so there is no evidence on alpha/zero-init/imbalance in this family.
labels_and_loss: [1] L2 end-point error between predicted and ground-truth Sintel flow (dense regression), no identity labels, no negatives. [2] MSE on z-scored velocities + binary cross-entropy on song probabilities; class imbalance handled by sampling at most 600,000 frames per LC type/control and balanced batches; the 'labels' that constrain units are the genetic perturbations. [3] none (forward simulation). [4] squared error on object centroid and velocity (single object). [5] none. [7] cross-entropy classification (ImageNet, skin disease etc.); similar classes (eczema/psoriasis) appear only as confusions. [8] none for FlyVis (cosine nearest-legend). Ours (prepared): cross-entropy over real same-class regions of tau x mean target response inside each region, i.e. the target region vs its real neighbours = hard negatives by construction; eligible queries require >= 2 real regions with all identities known. No source uses identity, pair, triplet or contrastive labels with a connectome-constrained model; hard negatives (similar neighbours) are not handled anywhere in this family.
data_camera_resolution_rate: [1] Sintel (23 training sequences, rendered CGI, moving virtual camera), 19-frame clips at 24 Hz upsampled to dt 20 ms, 721 columns (31 across), augmentation flips/rotations; validation on 26 published physiology studies (flash, moving edges). [2] Real courtship: 23 silenced LC types + controls, n > 12 sessions per type; test 27,000 frames (15 min of 3-s windows) per condition, ~11.6 million training samples; 30 fps-equivalent (10 frames ~300 ms); 64x228 grey reconstructions; no real camera, no lighting variation; calcium imaging of 5 LC types (LC6, LC11, LC12, LC15, LC17) for validation. [3] FlyWire v630 connectome, 127,400 neurons; 30 simulations of 1000 ms per experiment; validation by optogenetics and calcium imaging, 164 tested predictions. [4] DAVIS-2016 480p, 8 selected static-camera sequences, 24 fps, 10-frame blocks, 2 test blocks per sequence. [5] Simulated arena, 500 Hz rendering, 721 ommatidia per eye, flat or 'blocks' terrain, 11 trials per condition. [8] 400 DEV synthetic drawing sheets, 64x64 windows, 12-frame trajectories. None uses real driving-like video, low light, glare or crowded scenes of similar objects; [4] is the only one with real video and it deliberately excludes moving-camera sequences. Ours: BDD100K MOT, train_cache 130 videos (fit104 = fit84 + fit20) + train26, moving camera, night/glare, grey eye crop around the tracker prediction.
metrics_and_numbers: Authors' metrics, not transferable to our utility or HOTA. [1] (PMC11525180): 734 free parameters = 65 + 65 + 604; 45,669 neurons, 1,513,231 connections, 721 columns; task-performance vs direction-selectivity prediction across the 50-model ensemble r = 0.60, P = 2.6e-6 (Results 'Connectome and task are both necessary', Extended Data Fig. 2e); flash-response index did not improve with task performance (ED Fig. 2e); T4c clusters with average task error 5.297 (correct upward tuning), 5.316 (opposite), 5.357 (untuned) (Fig. 3); unconstrained CNN ensemble (5 models, 414,666 parameters each) used only as a lower bound on task error, value not stated in text (Methods). [6] FlyHack Table 1: common Sintel l2 score flyvis mean 1132.7 vs task-matched causal CNNs 1098.7 (small), 1040.6 (medium), 1028.8 (large), zero-flow 1209.6 (lower is better; authors note flyvis split not demonstrably held out); preferred directions within 45 deg for 190/400 T4/T5 subtypes (Section 7); T4/T5 output silencing reduces flow behaviour score to <= 2/8 clips in 40/50 models (Table 4). [4] Tschopp Fig. 7 / Section 4.1: test position error as low as 2.0 ommatidia; connectome weights frozen (bias + decoder only) worst at 2.6 ommatidia; velocity error 0.28-0.33 ommatidia/step; random sign-constrained init 'also able to track objects' (Section 4.3) but without T4 direction/orientation selectivity (Section 4.2). [2] Cowley Fig. 1f: held-out R2 forward velocity 0.50, lateral velocity 0.17; Fig. 2e: average noise-corrected R2 to real LC responses ~0.35 for knockout training, significantly better than dropout, no-knockout and untrained networks (P < 0.05, paired one-sided permutation, n = 27); ~0.65 with a fitted linear map from all model LC units (ED Fig. 8); FlyWire analysis Fig. 5b-c: 60.2% of presynaptic types project to >= 2 LC types, 45.7% to >= 3; Li32 projects to 27/28 LC types. [3] Shiu preprint Discussion: 91% of 164 tested predictions consistent, 84% excluding the split-GAL4 optogenetic screen. [8] Kuklev Tables 1-4: frozen fly + drift 0.857, receptors-only (no connectome) 0.891, repeated centre frame (no motion) 0.727 on 200 sheets, Gabor 0.802, pixel statistics 0.691, task-trained 5,888-parameter CNN 0.959 (3 seeds). [7] ConnectomeX Table 3: ImageNet-1K top-1 FlyVision-Large 66.25% vs ResNet18 69.25% (no connectome ablation). Ours for reference (runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json, paired per video, train26 n = 26): true_identity - baseline +2.836 pp [+1.873; +3.831]; appearance (base) - baseline +0.660 [+0.035; +1.302]; base_D - base +0.106 [-0.176; +0.400]; base_D - base_R1 -0.042 [-0.358; +0.280]; base_D - base_C -0.095 [-0.403; +0.228].
distinguishing_ablations: [1] Connectome-and-task ablations (ED Fig. 2a-d): random-parameter DMNs with the full connectome predict contrast preference but give poor direction selectivity/preferred direction; trained models with cell-type connectivity only predict activity poorly; signs suffice for contrast preference; direction selectivity (not preferred direction) achievable without synapse counts; merging T4/T5 subtypes harmless; merging all types into 3 groups ~ random DMN. These isolate the connectome's value for BIOLOGICAL FIDELITY, not for task performance: the only unconstrained comparison (CNN, 414,666 parameters) is described as a lower bound on task error, i.e. the connectome model is not claimed to be better at the task. The ensemble shows that task loss differences between local optima are tiny (5.297 vs 5.357) while internal tuning differs qualitatively. [4] Connectome vs random sign-constrained init on single-object DAVIS tracking: both track; only connectome init yields T4-like tuning; freezing connectome weights and training only biases and decoder is worst (2.6 vs 2.0 ommatidia) - closest analogue to 'how much do core parameters matter for a new object task': they do matter for task error, but the random-wiring control does about as well, so the gain is from trainable capacity, not from the connectome. [6] Equal-task CNN controls (small model roughly parameter-matched per authors): CNNs have lower flow error than flyvis; no evidence that connectome constraints improve task performance. [8] Receptors-only beats the full fly network (0.891 vs 0.857) and a 5,888-parameter task-trained CNN beats both (0.959): for a discrimination-among-similar-patterns task, frozen FlyVis processing adds nothing over its own eye input - same pattern as our base_D - base_R1 = -0.042 pp. [2] Knockout vs dropout vs no-knockout vs untrained, same architecture, same data, 10 seeds each: knockout gives better neural prediction (Fig. 2e) and more consistent solutions (ED Fig. 6); this is a training-procedure ablation, not a connectome or strong-base ablation. [7] No connectome ablation at all. No source contains the ablation we need: strong appearance base vs base + connectome-constrained branch vs base + equal-capacity unconstrained branch, nor any identity-among-distractors task. Negative/null results found: [4] random init tracks as well; [6] CNNs better on flow; [8] receptors-only better; FlyVis D = stock C in our project.
explanations_addressed: (a) Fly features carry no unique identity information beyond appearance: indirect support. [1] trains only on optic flow; nothing in the objective rewards encoding object identity, and [8] shows frozen FlyVis adds nothing over its receptor input for similar-pattern discrimination; our R1 control result is the same pattern - design caution, not direct evidence on our data. (b) Information exists but fusion/training ignores it (modality imbalance): only an analogy - [2] Methods report that adding 'slack' units lets the network ignore the constrained knocked-out units; no source fuses a fly branch with a strong base. (c) Saved readout features lost it; new activity or fine-tuned core needed: [4] is the only evidence that training the core parameters for a new object task matters (frozen connectome weights 2.6 vs trained 2.0 ommatidia), but the random-init control also solves it, so any gain from fine-tuning is expected to be capacity, not connectome - our rules then require the equal-capacity no-fly control; [1]'s ensemble shows many near-equivalent optima, so 734 per-type parameters move tuning a lot at small task cost - fine-tuning can change features, unknown whether toward identity. Our own prior core adaptations (z13_core_continue_v1: D-train - D-frozen -1.67 pp [-4.11; +0.83]; z13_aligned_core_v1 primary_pass false) were negative for localisation - caution. (d) FlyVis lacks the biological object/identity pathway (lobula): direct design support. [1] models only the motion pathway (64-65 types, Takemura fib25/fib19 connectome, no LC/LPLC); [2] places the object/female representation in the LC/LPLC bottleneck and finds a combinatorial population code over 23 LC types (position, size, rotation and their interactions ~25% variance), with FlyWire showing LC types share inputs (Li32 -> 27/28 LC types); [5] uses T2, T2a, T3, Tm, TmY as upstream partners of LC9/LC10 for fly following. None of them encodes individual identity among similar objects; LC codes in [2] describe a single female's geometry. (e) Motion helps only in subsets (darkness, glare, occlusion, similar look) diluted by averaging: not addressed (no source has such regimes). (f) Ceiling too low (+2.8 pp perfect identity vs +2 pp threshold): not addressed by sources; arithmetic from our report: appearance already takes +0.660 of the +2.836 perfect-identity utility, leaving ~2.18 pp; see math_precheck.
evidence_strength: [1] peer-reviewed Nature, code and 50 models public and used locally (verified config), independent re-analysis [6] confirms the released models run but questions task superiority and robustness of mechanistic claims: strong for 'connectome + flow task -> biological tuning', weak/none for 'connectome helps a new task'. [2] peer-reviewed Nature, code URL stated, 10 seeds, strong for knockout-training method but not connectome-constrained and single-object stimuli: moderate relevance. [3] peer-reviewed (Nature 2024; preprint read), no visual task, no training: low relevance. [4] arXiv work-in-progress, 8 DAVIS sequences, one run per configuration: weak. [5] Nature Methods, qualitative fly-following trials (11 per case): weak for identity. [6], [7], [8] 2026 single-group preprints, [7] and [8] without usable code: weak. Overall for the C08 question (can fine-tuning a connectome-constrained model help discrimination among similar objects, and do constraints beat an equal unconstrained network): weak - no direct study exists; the available ablations point the other way (unconstrained or receptor-only controls match or beat).
difference_from_tried: Mostly no new mechanism. Fine-tuning the 734 free parameters on a downstream objective is exactly what [1] did for flow and what our prepared scripts/z13_core_identity_20261026.py does for target-region choice; our earlier core adaptations for localisation (z13_aligned_core_v1, z13_core_continue_v1) and K1 (fly_finetune_k1) already tried core training on other objectives and were negative or inconclusive. What the sources add that we have not tried: (1) using the 50-model ensemble spread (different local optima of the same 734 parameters) as a training-free probe of how much the core can move identity information - we use only D (modernised 000-based) and stock C; (2) the random-parameter / random-init connectome and equal-task unconstrained CNN controls of [1], [4], [6] as the reference for 'connectome helps' - our planned gate compares only to initial D and stock C, not to R1 or an equal-capacity unconstrained network; (3) a lobula/LC-like bottleneck layer between the 34 output types and the readout ([2], [5], [10]) - not tried; (4) knockout/cue-masking style training that forces the constrained units to carry the signal ([2]) - not tried, and no perturbation data exist for our task.
math_precheck: Recipe in four steps, each with a stop rule; steps 1 and 4 use only saved features on CPU, steps 2-3 need new FlyVis forward passes but no core training. Step 1 (saved features, CPU, minutes): headroom arithmetic and connectome-vs-eye check. From runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json: perfect identity - bench = +2.836 pp, appearance - bench = +0.660 pp, so the maximum any fly addition could add over appearance on train26 is ~2.18 pp. If the pre-registered +2 pp is measured against the bench, the fly addition must deliver >= +1.34 pp over appearance, i.e. ~61% of the remaining identity-driven utility; if it is measured against appearance, ~92% [uncertain: which reference the +2 pp criterion uses for the fly-over-appearance comparison]. Required identity-error reduction: on fit104 out-of-fold, rank the appearance-only scorer's wrong top-1 choices by their utility consequence and compute what fraction must be corrected to reach that utility (oracle: replace appearance choice with the true region only on the k cheapest-to-fix queries). Compare with an upper bound for the fly: error complementarity = fraction of appearance-wrong queries where D alone (and separately R1 alone, C alone) ranks the true region first; oracle switch utility = utility when choosing D's answer exactly on those queries. Stop rule: if the oracle switch for D minus the oracle switch for R1 is <= 0 or the oracle switch for D gives less than the required utility, the existing representation cannot reach the criterion with any fusion; fine-tuning must then create new information. Step 2 (ensemble-spread probe, no training; new FlyVis maps with the 50 released models 000-049, same crops, same 68-feature readout): following [1], the 50 models are different local optima of the same 734 parameters with near-equal flow loss but qualitatively different tuning (T4c clusters 5.297/5.316/5.357). For each model k compute the conditional gain over appearance + R1 on fit104 with nested folds: delta log-loss (conditional V-information) and out-of-fold offline utility. The spread across k is a training-free estimate of how far 734-parameter changes move identity information. Stop rule: if the best model (selected on fit104, then checked once on fit20 not train26) has conditional gain over appearance + R1 with lower 95% bound <= 0 and point estimate below 25% of the step-1 requirement, do not run GPU core fine-tuning; the ensemble already samples the reachable parameter neighbourhood [uncertain: fine-tuning on identity can leave the flow-optimal set, so this is a heuristic bound, not a proof]. Step 3 (linearised fine-tuning / tangent probe, bounded GPU or CPU minutes, no training): at D compute Jacobian-vector products of the 68 regional features w.r.t. r = 16-32 parameter directions (the top singular directions of the per-query identity-loss gradients on fit84, scaled to the attraction-penalty radius of the prepared script); append the r x 68 directional features to [appearance, D] in the same nested boosting/logistic probe and evaluate on fit20. This upper-bounds what a first-order step of the prepared fine-tuning can add. Stop rule: if the conditional log-loss gain of the tangent block over [appearance, D] has CI including 0 and fit20 top-1 change < +0.03 (GATE_MIN of the prepared script), the 300-step run is unlikely to pass its own gate. Step 4 (equal-capacity control, CPU): train on saved R1 features (eye input) a small unconstrained model of 734 parameters (e.g. 68->10->1 MLP with region pooling, or ridge on R1 random features) with the same identity loss; its conditional gain over appearance is the 'addition without fly' arm. Proceed to GPU fine-tuning only if steps 1-3 leave room and the planned fine-tuned D must later beat this arm, not only initial D and stock C.
cue_role_and_regime: In [1] the core is a feature extractor whose 34 output types feed a decoder (feature role); in [5] the same outputs enter a z-scored saliency map that localises the only moving object (detection/selector role, regime: one target on a static background); in [2] LC units form a non-negative bottleneck integrating 10 frames, i.e. a per-object temporal state feeding behaviour (feature role, regime: one object, varying position/size/rotation); in [4] the core regresses one object's position and velocity (state/regression role). None targets the regime that matters for us - several same-class similar-looking detections near the predicted box, crossings, occlusion, darkness/glare. For our bench the fine-tuned core would enter as a per-candidate feature (mean target response inside each real region after a ridge target filter from the exemplar) for the identity stage; a gain measured on the fly-alone top-1 among regions (prepared gate) says nothing about the regime where MASA is wrong, so the check must be conditional on MASA and stratified by appearance-confusable queries (MASA top-1 wrong or margin small) and by night/glare videos.
no_fly_equivalent_control: Required arms for the three-way rule, with equal training (same fit84 queries, same loss, same steps, same readout): (1) appearance only (MASA) - base; (2a) appearance + eye input R1 with the same ridge readout and boosting (already exists: base_R1, D is -0.042 pp vs it); (2b) appearance + unconstrained network of equal size (~734 parameters) on R1 input, e.g. a hexagonal conv/recurrent layer with per-type-like parameter sharing, trained with the same cross-entropy over regions - analogue of [6]'s task-matched small CNN and [8]'s 5,888-parameter CNN; (2c) appearance + random-parameter connectome model trained identically (random DMN of [1] ED Fig. 2 / random sign-constrained init of [4]) - isolates the value of flow pretraining; (2d) optional degree-preserving shuffled connectome trained identically (listed as missing in [8]) - isolates topology; (3) appearance + fine-tuned D. A FlyVis result requires (3) > max(2a, 2b) with CI lower bound > 0; (3) > (2c) additionally supports flow-pretrained connectome parameters. Cheapest: 2a (exists) and 2b (CPU on saved R1 features if the identity readout is moved to region features; otherwise needs R1 crops which are cheap).
bio_node_mapping: Node = FlyVis core parameters (65 resting potentials, 65 time constants, 604 per-type-pair synapse strength scalings) on the Takemura fib25/fib19 'average filter' connectome (file fib25-fib19_v2.2.json in local _meta.yaml), and its 34 output types (T1-T5 incl. T4a-d/T5a-d, Tm, TmY). The object/identity-relevant downstream stage is the lobula LC/LPLC bottleneck ([2]: 57 LC/LPLC types, ~3.5% of brain neurons; LC10a/LC9 for tracking the female; LC11 small moving spots; LPLC2 loom), absent from FlyVis. Connectome data exist: FlyWire 783 (project copy data/flywire/783) contains LC types with presynaptic Tm/TmY/T2/T3/Li partners ([2] Fig. 5b; [5] upstream partners of LC9/LC10). Shiu [3] shows a whole-brain FlyWire LIF model is feasible with a single free weight, but it was not used for vision.
novelty_overlap: Nearest: [5] uses frozen FlyVis outputs to detect and follow one fly, [2] maps LC units to object features for one female, [4] fine-tunes a connectome model on single-object DAVIS tracking; none fine-tunes a connectome-constrained fly model for choosing the target among similar detections over a strong appearance base, which is our version (doubt noted, work not stopped).
candidate_node_change: Option A (core parameters, already prepared): run scripts/z13_core_identity_20261026.py only if math_precheck steps 1-3 leave room; modify its gate before the run (record as 'added before the run, reason: C08 controls') to (i) report the fit20 conditional gain over appearance (MASA cosines) rather than fly-alone top-1 only, (ii) add arms R1 + same ridge readout and an equal-size unconstrained 734-parameter network trained with identical loss/steps, (iii) optionally a random-parameter DMN trained identically. Why it targets a FlyVis problem: the core was optimised for flow only ([1]), so its outputs need not separate a target from same-class neighbours. Proceed to GPU when: precheck passes and the pilot shows new D - initial D >= +0.03 top-1 with lower bound > 0 AND new D beats R1 and the unconstrained control conditional on MASA; otherwise record negative and do not regenerate features. Option B (new readout node = lobula-like layer, part of our fly version): add a small non-negative LC-like bottleneck (10-23 units per region, ReLU, temporal integration over the last frames as in [2]) on the 34 output types, with input masks/initial weights from FlyWire 783 synapse counts from T2/T2a/T3/Tm/TmY to LC9/LC10/LC11/LC15/LC17-like types; core frozen; trained with cross-entropy over real regions on fit84; controls: same layer with dense unmasked weights (equal size), same layer on R1, appearance only. Cue-masking/knockout analogue: randomly drop the MASA input during training of the fused head so the LC units must carry identity on their own (inspired by [2]'s argument that spare capacity lets a network ignore constrained units). Proceed to GPU only if the CPU version on saved 68-feature activity (pooled per region) shows conditional gain over appearance + R1 with lower bound > 0 on fit104 out-of-fold.
strongest_objection: No study in this family shows that connectome constraints or core fine-tuning help a task other than the one the core was built for, and every available control points the other way: in [4] a randomly initialised sign-constrained network solved single-object tracking about as well; in [6] task-matched CNNs beat FlyVis on its own flow task; in [8] the receptor input beat the frozen fly network on discriminating similar patterns; in our project D = C and D is not better than R1 given MASA. [1]'s evidence for the connectome is about biological fidelity (r = 0.60 between task performance and DS prediction), not about task performance, and identity among similar objects is not a computation of the optic-lobe motion pathway at all ([2] places object coding in LC units outside FlyVis). Hence fine-tuning 734 per-type parameters is likely to produce, at best, a capacity gain that an equal-size unconstrained network on R1 reproduces - which under the project rule would not be a FlyVis result.
cost_and_hardware: Step 1 and step 4 of math_precheck: CPU, minutes, on saved runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_{C,D,R1}.npz (8326 queries x 18 regions x 238 features) and the corresponding fit104 features. Step 2 (50-model ensemble maps): new FlyVis forward passes for 50 checkpoints on the same crops of fit104 (+ fit20) - inference only, one 12 GB GPU, estimated several GPU hours [uncertain: depends on the measured per-model feature-generation time of earlier D/C runs]; can be cut to the 10 best models as in [1]. Step 3 (tangent probe): r = 16-32 JVPs per sampled query on ~1000 fit84/fit20 queries, under one GPU hour [uncertain]. Option A fine-tuning: 300 steps x 8 episodes on one GPU, within one night window (deadline handled by the prepared script). Option B LC-like layer: CPU on saved pooled activity first; GPU only for regenerating spatial activity maps.
